Second Phase 2 run — independent re-audit of fix commit d1bf2cb, which claimed to resolve all 7 CRITICAL and 8 HIGH findings from the first run. 13 of 15 claims independently VERIFIED as genuine, non-trivial fixes (6 confirm() dialogs with specific messages verified present; MFA fieldset/labels verified; responsive hamburger + 11/11 tables wrapped verified; pagination verified with correct range math on 3 of 4 target files; N+1 email resolution verified fixed; user-detail single-row lookup verified; 25 real passing tests added for JWT/PKCE/middleware; structured logger + instrumentation verified wired through all 12 auth-server routes). Verdict unchanged from the first run (NOT PRODUCTION READY) despite substantial real progress, because any open CRITICAL caps the verdict regardless of how much else improved.

Third Phase 2 run — narrowly scoped, independent re-audit of migration 0026 (commit b45ab5d), which claimed to close the last-owner-lockout gap PQ-SEC-003/PQ-SEC-004 exposed in memberships DELETE/UPDATE. Both independently live-tested and VERIFIED resolved against the running local Supabase sandbox, including a multi-role-membership edge case not previously tested. While probing the edge cases this run's scope specifically named (multiple roles, organization_id changes, non-org-deletion cascades), found ONE new, narrower gap: the UPDATE trigger never checks organization_id changes, only status — live-exploited under a dual-org-admin precondition (confirmed NOT exploitable by a single-org Admin, since RLS's implicit WITH CHECK already blocks that narrower case), tracked as new HIGH finding PQ-SEC-005, not CRITICAL given the materially narrower precondition than PQ-SEC-003/004. No conflict found between migration 0026 and the existing 0025 (membership_roles) or 0024 (audit-log) triggers — BEFORE/AFTER ordering cleanly separates the last-owner guard from audit logging, and 0025's cascade-safety no-op correctly engages once 0026's trigger has already removed the parent row. Per user's explicit, deliberate scope decision this run, the 4 HIGH findings from the second run (PQ-UX-007, PQ-PERF-001, PQ-TECH-001, PQ-TECH-002) were accepted as documented technical debt and carried forward unchanged rather than re-verified in depth. Verdict improves from NOT PRODUCTION READY to FUNCTIONAL MVP now that both CRITICALs are closed, but Phase 2 still cannot PASS today: 5 HIGH findings remain open (1 new, 4 deliberately deferred), and the gate's own rule requires zero open HIGH/CRITICAL for PASS.

Per this round's explicit instruction to 'check hard' for any remaining last-owner-protection bypass beyond what runs 2/3 had ruled out, deliberately tested operations none of migrations 0025/0026/0027 constrain (role-assignment INSERT, membership user_id UPDATE) rather than re-testing the same delete/status/org-reassignment operations again. Found and live-exploited TWO NEW CRITICAL findings that together fully defeat the entire day's last-owner-protection effort via a precondition strictly weaker than PQ-SEC-005's: PQ-SEC-006 (a plain org Admin can self-promote to Owner via an unrestricted membership_roles INSERT, migration 0010, never touched by any fix today — live-chained end-to-end with the legitimate 2-owner suspend path to fully lock out the real Owner) and PQ-SEC-007 (a plain org Admin can silently reassign an Owner membership's user_id to any arbitrary platform user via an unrestricted memberships UPDATE, also migration 0010 — a complete, untraceable organization takeover, since the audit trigger only logs status changes). Both root causes pre-date today entirely and were not introduced by any commit today; they were simply never tested by three prior same-day rounds that all focused on the delete/status/org-reassignment surface. Verdict returns to NOT PRODUCTION READY: 2 CRITICAL findings are open, and per the gate's own rules an open CRITICAL caps the verdict regardless of how much else has genuinely improved (all 5 HIGH findings from the third run are now closed; only 1 HIGH remains, plus 24 MEDIUM). Phase 2 is NOT closing today.
